scams.name: Mexico City-to-Puebla Bus Terminal Taxi Scam (TAPO + CAPU)
scams.description: Mexico City-to-Puebla bus transit is one of Mexico's busiest tourist corridors (2-hour ride, MX$200-300 ADO primera-clase). The transit zones at both TAPO and CAPU host 2025 taxi and fake-ticket scams. A June 2025 traveler report documents a ~US$600 loss at a TAPO taxi sitio, with adjacent 2025 reports covering police shakedowns outside Mexico City Airport and Uber-to-Puebla toll dynamics. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) TAPO 'sitio' counters inside terminal selling rides at MX$400-800 to central Mexico City when Uber/Didi is MX$120-250; (b) counterfeit bus-ticket resellers outside TAPO or CAPU selling 'ADO Primera Clase discount' at fake barcodes; (c) credit-card cloning at 'sitio' counter handing card 'for deposit'; (d) CAPU arrival taxi quoting MX$500-800 to Centro Histórico Puebla (real Uber MX$100-180 for 15 km); (e) bus-station 'luggage helper' demanding MX$200 per bag; (f) 'combined Mexico City-Puebla-Cholula tour US$200' bundle at TAPO (real ADO+Uber+Cholula Uber round-trip <US$60 independent); (g) WhatsApp-based 'cheap bus tickets' from scalpers outside CAPU. For older travelers: (1) for Mexico City-to-Puebla, buy ADO tickets at the OFFICIAL counter inside TAPO OR on ado.com.mx — MX$250-300 Primera Plus/Clase (2-hour comfortable ride); (2) alternatively Estrella Roja at ado.com.mx also safe; (3) at TAPO for your return to CDMX, use Uber on MAIN STREET outside terminal (NOT 'sitio' inside) — typical Mexico City Centro MX$120-250; (4) at CAPU Puebla arrival, use Uber on the main street — CAPU to Centro Histórico Puebla is MX$100-180 via Uber, MX$60-80 via colectivo; (5) NEVER buy bus tickets from resellers outside terminals; (6) NEVER hand credit card to any 'sitio' counter; (7) REFUSE 'combined Mexico City-Puebla-Cholula tour US$200' — DIY is <US$60 total; (8) traveler reports provide specific defense scripts for TAPO; (9) save Puebla Tourist Police +52 222 237 2211.
scams.avoidance: ADO ticket at official counter inside TAPO or ado.com.mx: MX$250-300 At TAPO/CAPU, use Uber from MAIN STREET outside terminal CAPU-Puebla Centro: Uber MX$100-180 or colectivo MX$60-80 NEVER buy tickets from resellers; never hand card to sitio Puebla Tourist Police +52 222 237 2211
scams.location: Mexico City TAPO bus terminal, Puebla CAPU bus terminal (Central de Autobuses de Puebla), ADO + Estrella Roja ticket windows, fake-ticket resellers

scams.name: Puebla Cholula 'Mandatory Archaeological Guide' & Great Pyramid Scam
scams.description: The Great Pyramid of Cholula is the world's LARGEST pyramid by volume (larger than Giza) with a Spanish church built on top and a 10-km network of excavation tunnels. It's Puebla's iconic day-trip — 20-minute drive from Centro Puebla — and hosts a 2025 mandatory-guide + entry-fee padding scam. Traveler reports cover the Cholula day-trip logistics. Legitimate costs: Great Pyramid of Cholula INAH entry is MX$95 for foreigners (includes tunnel access + archaeological zone + museum). Optional licensed guides at the ticket booth charge MX$400-800 PER GROUP (4-8 people), not per person. Church on top (Iglesia Nuestra Señora de los Remedios) is FREE entry (climb up via pyramid path included in ticket). The 2025 scam patterns: (a) 'mandatory tunnel guide MX$500 per person' claim at entrance — no guide is required; tunnel path is self-guided with posted maps; (b) 'premium archaeological tour MX$1,500' ticket resellers online for basic entrance; (c) 'church entrance fee MX$100' demanded at the top (church is FREE); (d) 'parking fee MX$300' at unofficial lots near entrance (real official parking MX$50); (e) 'mandatory donation for archaeological preservation MX$200' at exit (no such fee); (f) 'photo package MX$400' upsells from 'official' photographers (fake); (g) 'combined Cholula + Puebla tour MX$2,000 per person' bundled tours with commission restaurants; (h) 'tunnel closed for restoration, special access MX$300' (tunnels are always open during published hours). For older travelers: (1) buy Cholula Pyramid entry at the OFFICIAL INAH window — MX$95 foreigner rate includes tunnels + zone + museum + church-top access; (2) park at the official lot MX$50; (3) NO mandatory guide — free self-guided maps available at ticket office; optional licensed guides MX$400-800 PER GROUP; (4) REFUSE every 'mandatory guide', 'church entry', 'archaeological donation', 'photo package' demand; (5) arrive at 9 AM opening before tour buses; allow 2-3 hours for full visit (tunnel network + pyramid + church + museum); (6) tunnels are 800m/kombi-size passages — older travelers should bring hat (head-bump hazard), torch/phone flashlight (lighting is dim), comfortable walking shoes; (7) for Cholula town center afterwards, walk 1 km north to Zócalo de Cholula for lunch at Café Colonial, Los Caporales (Google 4.7+); (8) return to Puebla via Uber MX$150-200 each way (20 min); (9) skip 'combined Cholula + Puebla tour' bundles — DIY is far better value.
scams.avoidance: Pay ONLY MX$95 at INAH window (includes tunnels + church + museum) Park at official lot MX$50; NO mandatory guide REFUSE 'mandatory guide', 'church entry', 'donation', 'photos' demands Arrive 9 AM opening; 2-3 hours for full visit Return to Puebla via Uber MX$150-200 (20 min); DIY beats bundles
scams.location: Great Pyramid of Cholula (Tlachihualtépetl), Iglesia de los Remedios (church on top), entrance ticket office, parking lot, tunnel tour kiosks

scams.name: Puebla Talavera Pottery 'Authentic Certified' Fake Pricing & Workshop Scam
scams.description: Puebla is Mexico's Talavera ceramics capital and hosts a 2025 fake-certified-authentic + workshop-visit commission scam. Traveler reports from 2025 document the overall Mexico-travel scam landscape that includes these patterns. Legitimate Talavera: REAL certified Talavera Poblana has the 'DO4' (Denominación de Origen) stamp and requires a 2-step kiln-firing process that takes months. Certified producers: Uriarte Talavera (1824 heritage, fair prices MX$800-$8,000 for dinnerware/decorative), Talavera de la Reyna, La Casa del Cafe, Talavera Armando — all have visible DO4 certification on each piece. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) El Parián and Centro shops selling 'authentic Talavera' at MX$2,000-$6,000 per piece that lacks DO4 stamp (often made in Oaxaca or imported Portuguese-style majolica — not real Talavera); (b) 'artist workshop tour US$40 per person' that's a commission shopping trip with high-pressure sales; (c) 'limited edition signed by master US$500' for mass-produced pieces; (d) 'FedEx international shipping to USA US$150' at 3-5x real rate with breakage risk; (e) 'damaged in transit' fraud at destination; (f) 'certificate of authenticity' printed sticker rather than kiln-embedded DO4 mark; (g) 'buy three get one free' pressure with inflated original; (h) credit-card 'manual entry' for deposit (cloning risk). For older travelers: (1) verify REAL Talavera via DO4 stamp KILN-EMBEDDED into piece (not sticker); (2) buy from certified producers: Uriarte Talavera (4 Norte 911), Talavera de la Reyna (Av. Puebla), La Casa del Cafe (6 Sur 301) — transparent pricing with certification; (3) REFUSE 'artist workshop tour US$40 per person' — commission shopping; visit Uriarte workshop for FREE during business hours; (4) fair prices: Talavera dinnerware 10-piece set MX$3,500-8,000, decorative plate MX$800-2,500, small tile MX$50-150 per piece; (5) NEVER buy from El Parián market stalls (most lack DO4 certification); (6) for international shipping, use certified FedEx/DHL office direct (not shop 'shipping service'); (7) NEVER use 'manual entry' credit-card swipe; (8) pay cash for small items; credit card at legitimate POS only.
scams.avoidance: Verify DO4 stamp KILN-EMBEDDED into piece (not sticker) Certified: Uriarte Talavera, Talavera de la Reyna, La Casa del Cafe Uriarte workshop FREE tour during business hours (no US$40 fee) International shipping via certified FedEx/DHL office direct NEVER use 'manual entry' credit-card swipe
scams.location: Puebla Centro Histórico Talavera workshops, El Parián craft market, Uriarte Talavera showroom area, tourist-trap 'authentic' galleries

scams.name: Puebla Centro Restaurant Tourist-Menu Bill-Padding & Chile en Nogada Upcharge
scams.description: Puebla is Mexico's gastronomic capital — mole poblano, chile en nogada (seasonal), cemitas, chalupas — and its Centro hosts a 2025 tourist-menu padding ecosystem. Traveler reports from 2025 document the overall Mexico-travel scam landscape. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Zócalo-perimeter restaurants with USD-priced English menus at 2-3x local prices (mole poblano US$18 vs MX$150 at working-class spots); (b) 'chile en nogada special MX$600' during season (July-September) at tourist-menu spots (real MX$250-350 at authentic restaurants); (c) 'gratuity 18% included' + tip line (double-tipping); (d) credit-card surcharge 10-15% announced at bill; (e) 'imported Spanish wine' at MX$1,200 per bottle for Mexican varietals labelled differently; (f) 'market price' verbal quotes on barbacoa or cabrito without weight disclosed; (g) 'complimentary appetizer' arriving as MX$280 line item; (h) tour-bus commission restaurants adding 'mariachi surcharge MX$100/person' to the bill. For older travelers: (1) eat AUTHENTIC Poblano at: Fonda de Santa Clara (3 Poniente 307, Google 4.6+, MX$200-400 per person), El Mural de los Poblanos (16 de Septiembre 506), La Noria (Tlatelolco 4 Norte 106), Sacristía de la Compañía (6 Sur 304) — all reputable with transparent pricing; (2) for chile en nogada (July-Sept only), fair price is MX$250-350 per plate; (3) for cemitas (Puebla's signature sandwich), try Las Poblanitas de Tepeaca or Tortas Las Mil Delicias for authentic MX$50-90; (4) chalupas at Plazuela de los Sapos on weekends for MX$15-25 per chalupa; (5) INSPECT bill — 'gratuity 18%' means NO additional tip; confirm credit-card surcharge 0-3% BEFORE ordering; (6) request MX$ bill not USD; (7) refuse 'complimentary' appetizers arriving uninvited; (8) for special-occasion dining at pricier venues (Meson Sacristía, El Mural): budget MX$600-1,000 per person all-in, worth it for authenticity; (9) skip Zócalo-perimeter tourist-menu restaurants; (10) traveler reports list 2025 Puebla restaurant recommendations.
scams.avoidance: Eat authentic: Fonda de Santa Clara, El Mural de los Poblanos, La Noria Chile en Nogada (July-Sept only) fair MX$250-350 Cemitas at Las Poblanitas de Tepeaca MX$50-90 Inspect bill; refuse double-tipping; card surcharge 0-3% max Request MX$ bill (not USD); refuse uninvited appetizers
scams.location: Puebla Centro Histórico Av. 5 de Mayo, Zócalo restaurant perimeter, El Parián area, tourist-menu spots targeting CDMX day-trippers

scams.name: Puebla Day-Trip Driver & Hotel-Concierge Commission Kickbacks
scams.description: Puebla is a popular 2-3 day side trip from Mexico City with multiple day-trip destinations (Cholula, Atlixco, Africam Safari, Cantona ruins), and hosts a 2025 tour-commission + concierge-kickback ecosystem. Traveler reports from 2025 cover Mexico travel broadly and driver-hire pricing from CDMX to Puebla. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) hotel-concierge 'recommended driver' at MX$3,500 per day vs Uber day-hire MX$1,500-2,000; (b) 'combined Puebla + Cholula + Atlixco tour US$150 per person' bundled with commission stops (real DIY MX$600-800 total via Uber); (c) tour-bus driver directing to specific 'artisan' shops / restaurants for kickback; (d) 'Africam Safari shuttle US$90 per person round-trip' when Uber is MX$400 one-way; (e) 'private driver with lunch' packages at MX$4,500 (MX$800 lunch in reality); (f) 'VIP access to Cantona archaeological site US$200' (real entry MX$70); (g) 'photograph package US$60' during tours; (h) 'tip not included US$30 expected' pressure at tour end. For older travelers: (1) for Cholula: Uber from Puebla Centro MX$150-200 one-way (20 min); (2) for Atlixco (pueblo mágico 30 km SW): Uber MX$300-400 one-way; (3) for Africam Safari: Uber MX$400 one-way (50-min drive); park entry MX$450 adult (fair direct rate); (4) for Cantona ruins: Uber MX$800 one-way (2-hour drive); entry MX$70 — long day trip; (5) book Google 4.7+ tours if preferred (Estrella Tours Puebla, Viajero Rodante) at MX$1,500-2,000 per person for full-day multi-stop; (6) REFUSE every 'combined Puebla + 3-stop tour US$150+' from hotel concierge; (7) if hiring private driver, negotiate BEFORE engaging: MX$1,500-2,000/day with lunch + gas fair; (8) for shorter day-trips, self-DIY via Uber is cheaper and more flexible; (9) traveler reports list 2025 Mexico-itinerary tips.
scams.avoidance: Uber self-DIY: Cholula MX$150-200, Atlixco MX$300-400, Africam MX$400 Google 4.7+ tours: Estrella Tours Puebla, Viajero Rodante MX$1,500-2,000 Negotiate private driver BEFORE engaging: MX$1,500-2,000/day fair REFUSE hotel-concierge 'combined tour US$150+' bundles DIY via Uber is cheaper and more flexible
scams.location: Puebla hotel-concierge desks, CAPU bus-station driver-for-hire, Centro Histórico tour operators, Cholula/Atlixco/Africam Safari day-trip routes

scams.name: Puebla ATM DCC & Centro Cash-Exchange Padding
scams.description: Puebla shares Mexico's 2025 ATM DCC fraud + exchange padding pattern. Traveler reports from Mexico City and Cancún provide the canonical DCC-fraud warning and the 2025 regional reference for USD-to-peso exchange. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Av. 5 de Mayo freestanding ATMs with 'home currency conversion?' DCC prompts at 8-15% padded rates; (b) hotel-lobby ATMs (Cardtronics, EuroNet) with MX$150-250 fees PLUS DCC; (c) Puebla airport currency exchange at 10-15% padded vs downtown rates; (d) Centro merchants adding 'foreign card surcharge MX$250' (illegitimate); (e) 'USD accepted here' pricing at MX$16 per US$1 when Bank of Mexico rate is MX$18.5 (13% padded); (f) cash-back at supermarkets at terrible rates; (g) casa de cambio on side streets off Av. 5 de Mayo with tampered calculators. For older travelers: (1) use ONLY ATMs INSIDE bank branches — HSBC, Banamex, Santander, BBVA, Banorte — located on Av. 5 de Mayo, Av. Juan de Palafox, during business hours (9 AM-4 PM Mon-Fri); (2) when ATM asks 'home currency conversion?', ALWAYS select 'NO' or 'Continue in MX Pesos'; (3) set LOW daily limits (MX$3,000) + transaction alerts; (4) for USD exchange, use reputable casa de cambio (Forex at Av. Palafox y Mendoza, Casa de Cambio DYNER), NOT hotel-reception; (5) AVOID airport currency exchange — downtown is 10-15% better; (6) for daily spending, tap-to-pay credit card — interbank rate 1-2% better than ATM; (7) dedicated travel debit card (not primary); (8) decline 'USD or MX$?' restaurant offers — always pay MX$-posted price; (9) RFID-blocking wallet for contactless cards; (10) if Puebla is part of a multi-day Mexico City trip, withdraw sufficient cash at CDMX bank-branch ATMs BEFORE travelling to avoid Puebla-specific issues.
scams.avoidance: Bank-branch ATMs only (HSBC, Banamex, Santander, BBVA, Banorte) ALWAYS select 'Continue in MX Pesos' on DCC prompt Exchange at Forex or Casa de Cambio DYNER downtown Set MX$3,000 daily limit + transaction alerts Pay MX$-posted price always; tap-to-pay credit card best
scams.location: Puebla Centro Histórico freestanding ATMs, Av. 5 de Mayo tourist-strip ATMs, hotel-lobby ATMs, airport currency kiosks
